title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting and purpose. This page continues the previous one. There, for a morphism u : A' → A of abelian varieties of the same dimension, Grothendieck showed that u^* on H^{2n} is multiplication by deg u. The purpose is to build up the cohomology and cycle-class formalism for abelian varieties needed for the standard conjectures (Lefschetz, Hodge, Tate) in that case.

On this page the notation is reversed and the dimensions are arbitrary:
- u : A → A' is a homomorphism of abelian varieties, with dim A = n and dim A' = n'.
- The 'm' in the transcription is almost certainly n.
- u_* : H^i(A) → H^{i+2(n'-n)}(A')(n'-n) is the Gysin map, defined by transposing u^* via Poincaré duality.

The claim has three parts.
- u_*(1_A) ∈ H^{2(n'-n)}(A')(n'-n) is the cohomology class of the image cycle u_*[A] ∈ C^{n'-n}(A'). This holds because the Gysin map is compatible with proper pushforward of cycles.
- Hence u_*(1_A) = 0 if dim u(A) < n.
- If u(A) = B has dimension n and d is the degree of A → B, then u_*(1_A) = d · γ_{A'}(B), the cycle class of B.

The same thing in linear algebra. Write V = T_ℓ(A) ⊗ Q_ℓ, so that H^1(A) = V^∨ and H^*(A) = ∧^* H^1(A). Let u_1 : V(A) → V(A') be the induced map.
- If u_1 is not injective (u has positive-dimensional kernel), the image of the top class ∧^{2n}V(A) is 0.
- If u_1 is injective, the image is a decomposable 2n-vector in ∧^{2n}V(A'). By the duality ∧^{2n}V' ≅ ∧^{2(n'-n)}V'^∨ ⊗ ∧^{2n'}V', it is the same as an alternating 2(n'-n)-form on V(A'). Here 2(n'-n) = dim coker u_1.
- That form is the class of d·B in ∧^{2(n'-n)}H^1(A') = H^{2(n'-n)}(A').

This is the standard description of the class of an abelian subvariety as a decomposable multivector, i.e. the Plücker point of its Tate module.
errors: Notational slips: the 'm' in H^{2(n'-m)} and C^{n'-m} must be n. The cycle u(A) lives in C^{n'-n}(A'), not C(A).

Imprecision: the decomposable multivector ∧^{2n}u_1(V(A)) is determined only up to the normalization of the orientation/fundamental classes. To recover the factor d integrally one must work with Z_ℓ-lattices, and even then only the ℓ-part of d is visible. Over Q_ℓ the statement holds once the scalar is fixed via the fundamental classes. This is not addressed.
'Not injective ⇒ 0' and 'injective ⇒ dim u(A) = n' are correct, since u_1 is injective iff ker u is finite.

ideas.what: Gysin pushforward of the fundamental class under a homomorphism of abelian varieties equals the degree times the cycle class of the image abelian subvariety
ideas.modern_name: Projection formula / cycle class compatibility with proper pushforward
ideas.where_published: Cycle class and Gysin formalism in SGA 4½ (Deligne) and SGA 5

ideas.what: The class of an abelian subvariety B ⊂ A' in ∧^{2c}H^1(A') is the decomposable multivector given by T_ℓ(B) ⊂ T_ℓ(A'), read as an alternating form via duality
ideas.modern_name: Cohomology class of an abelian subvariety as a Plücker/decomposable element of ∧^* H^1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (Lieberman; Kleiman's 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' 1968 on the standard conjectures for abelian varieties)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping in the cohomology of abelian varieties, standard in Lieberman/Kleiman-era treatments of the standard conjectures for abelian varieties. Nothing new. The next page is an unrelated typed text on sites.

'en figure générale' is probably 'de façon générale'.
'la U.A. image' is probably 'la V.A. image' (variété abélienne image).
'la transposée Cl. de Q_ℓ' is probably 'la transposée ... des Q_ℓ-modules de Tate', i.e. u_1 on T_{Q_ℓ}.
